title: Workload caging and adaptive throughput contracts for Dedicated GPU pools
creator: Ethan Morales
description:
Problem: Customers on Dedicated pools occasionally experience unpredictable tail latency and throughput drops due to bursty neighbors and cold autoscale paths. Existing soft-quota controls reduce severity but do not provide contractual throughput guarantees or predictable autoscale behavior for SLAs.

Proposed solution: Implement a workload caging system that composes three coordinated controls: (1) per-workload throughput contracts (expressed as tokens/sec + burst envelope) enforced at the scheduler and GPU slab level; (2) an adaptive autoscaler (stepped-hedge policy) that pre-warms additional lanes based on sustained contract pressure and a short predictive window; (3) a low-impact eviction and throttle guard that applies progressive penalties to offenders while preserving guaranteed throughput for contract-honored workloads.

Key design points:
- Contracts are hierarchical: tenant-level contract -> workload-group contract -> request route override. Contracts are represented as small immutable descriptors pinned to rollout versions.
- Enforcement uses a two-layer token bucket: a per-GPU slab bucket for aggregate capacity and a per-contract bucket for fairness. This reduces cross-tenant noise while allowing slack reuse within the slab.
- Autoscaler uses a stepped-hedge approach: minor sustained contract pressure triggers soft burst lanes (best-effort) for 30s; if pressure persists, escalate to reserved lanes with a cooldown and capacity pre-warm to avoid cold-start latency.
- Eviction/throttling is progressive and evidence-based: we score noisy workloads by sustained token overrun, KV cache miss amplification, and percentiles of latencies. Policy favors throttling degraded tailers over evicting workloads with active contracts.
- Observability: expose contract-level SLOs (throughput attainment, tail latency, preemptions) to Console with token-level cost attribution and an alert rule set for contract breach.

Trade-offs considered:
- Strict hard-slicing guarantees absolute isolation but reduces utilization and increases cost; we choose hierarchical token contracts to balance utilization with predictable throughput.
- Predictive autoscaling reduces latency but can overshoot; the stepped-hedge minimizes overshoot with cooldowns and conservative pre-warm sizing.

Rollout plan: feature-flagged rollout starting in a single region and two pilot customers on Dedicated (non-critical workloads). Gradual enable of enforcement from monitoring-only -> soft-throttle -> strict enforcement over 4 weeks.

Docs/Artifacts: Confluence design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/DED/Workload+Caging+Design, GitHub RFC: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rfcs/pull/219, Prototype PR (scheduler changes): https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/6142
acceptance_criteria: Contracts can be created and attached to a Dedicated capacity allocation via API and Console
Scheduler enforces per-contract token buckets and per-GPU slab buckets without deadlocks or priority inversion
Autoscaler responds with stepped-hedge pre-warm behavior and respects cooldowns in 95% of simulated burst scenarios
Noisy neighbor incidents (measured as percent of requests delayed >2x baseline) drop by >=60% in pilot clusters
Contract-level metrics surface in Console: contract_throughput, contract_breach_count, contract_tail_latency
Security review completed and KMS-backed contract descriptors validated for tamper-resistance
comments: 2026-02-16 - Ethan Morales: Initial design draft posted to Confluence. Raised question about how to represent contracts in the existing model catalog. Suggested immutable descriptors pinned to model/version IDs.

2026-02-19 - Lena Ortiz: Implemented a prototype token-bucket shim in the scheduler branch. Observed low contention in microbenchmarks but saw increased latency during cold lane spin-up. Proposed stepped-hedge autoscaler to mitigate.

2026-02-22 - Marcus Nguyen (review): Reviewed prototype. Concern: if per-contract buckets are too strict, we may starve non-contracted traffic. Recommendation: allow conservative spare capacity reuse with a reclaimable tag and an observed reclaim policy.

2026-02-25 - Security review kickoff (Priya Shah): Noted that contract descriptors must be integrity-protected when replicated across control plane instances. PR for KMS signing added to repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/security/pull/88

2026-03-01 - SRE (Asha Patel): Load test results for pilot cluster attached to dashboard. Under mixed workloads we saw 65% fewer contract breaches after soft-throttle policy applied. Need more runs for the pre-warm sizing matrix.

2026-03-03 - Lena Ortiz: Updated scheduler PR to add a backoff window and fence flag to prevent priority inversion. Preparing canary plan to flip enforcement-on in region eu-west-1 for two pilot tenants next week.
2026-03-04 - Product (Ravi Desai): Endorsement: product OK with pilot. Request to add a billing telemetry event when reserved lanes are pre-warmed so customers can see cost impact in Console.

2026-03-04 - QA (Sofia Ivanova): Test plan created and linked. Will validate deterministic token behavior, autoscaler cooldowns, and chaos scenarios where an entire rack fails while pre-warmed lanes are active.
